A1.justification: Despite the changed title and author list, both PDFs describe the same weak-correlation framework, equivalence theorems, and SGD linearization bounds. All 42 pages of v1 and 43 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results, proofs, and mathematical network constructions, including Appendices A-F. Its empirical observations are attributed to prior work; no original experimental outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Figures 1-4 and Appendix A report original neural-network experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10, and Fashion-MNIST, measuring derivative correlations and discrepancies from linearized models.

M1.justification: v2 adds a directional-derivative procedure for computing correlation tensors without constructing full higher derivatives (Equation 13), and a sampled-weight approximation in Appendix A.1. These are limited computational additions; the SGD update, NTK formulation, and underlying theoretical network constructions remain.

E1.justification: v1 has no experimentally evaluated datasets. v2 introduces ten-class image experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10, and Fashion-MNIST in Appendix A.1, with additional MNIST experiments in Appendix A.2. This establishes substantial empirical dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The NTK/first-order Taylor linearization, discussed analytically in v1, becomes an actually evaluated reference model against nonlinear networks in Appendix A.1-A.2. The comparator addition is limited to this reference-model family.

E3.justification: v2 introduces NTK-normalized, small-subset experiments and a separate standard-parameterized GELU MLP protocol using 250 SGD steps, batch size 128, 14 widths, and five learning-rate scalings. These protocols are absent from v1. Appendix A.1's sample counts remain ambiguous: its text specifies 160 training and 32 test samples, while Figures 2-3 say 1160 samples.

E4.justification: New analyses examine correlation decay across widths, activations, and depths (Figure 1), nonlinear-versus-linearized discrepancy and third-order correlations across widths (Figures 2-3), and learning-rate-dependent scaling of linearization error (Figure 4). v1 contains no corresponding empirical sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 newly reports 100 seeds per configuration, shared randomness within nonlinear/linearized pairs, averaging, individual-seed displays, and log-log regression for scaling estimates. This introduces repeated-run and statistical-estimation reporting absent from v1. Confidence intervals and uncertainty estimates for fitted slopes are not provided.

E6.justification: v2 adds all experimental outcomes, including generally declining correlation magnitudes and linearization discrepancies with width, and learning-rate-dependent error scaling. These are new results, not improvements over earlier scores. Exact Figure 4 slopes are inconsistently reported: for alpha = -0.5, the caption gives approximately -1.3 while the plot legend gives -1.14.

T1.justification: The core theorems and proof framework are retained, with localized mathematical revisions. v2 changes min to max in the asymptotic-bound construction (v1 Equation 43; v2 Equation 55), corrects the gradient-deviation expression (v1 Equation 108; v2 Equation 120), and replaces inconsistent FCNN weak-correlation rate statements with sqrt(n)-based statements in Section 4.2 and Appendix G.4.

C1.justification: The five enumerated contributions and central equivalence and SGD-bound claims remain. v2 adds an explicit empirical-validation claim in the abstract and prospective claims in the conclusion about using the framework to guide model design.

C2.justification: Section 3.3.3 and new Appendix H substantially expand the bias interpretation, connecting derivative correlations to initialization correlations, parameter-space restrictions, and learning the model's own structure. Appendix A.2 also acknowledges disagreement with expected scaling and proposes finite-width and shared-data explanations. The original assumptions and limitations largely remain in Appendix I.

D1.justification: v2 adds experimental implementation details absent from v1: JAX and PyTorch/JVP procedures, preprocessing, hyperparameters, derivative sampling, hardware, and per-seed result logging. Appendix A.1 reports an Apple M1 Pro and approximately one hour of runtime; A.2 specifies an NVIDIA B200. Code sharing on GitHub is asserted, but no repository address is supplied.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 3.3.2 substantially expand positioning against Feynman-diagram methods, the neural tangent hierarchy, and weak-submodel explanations, discussing Dyer and Gur-Ari, Huang and Yau, and Liu et al. (2022). Six cited works are added while the earlier references are retained; these additions develop substantive relationships to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 extensively edits prose throughout the main text and proofs, changes the title and author list, and reorganizes the narrative. Much of Section 2's explanatory background moves to Appendix B, new experimental and interpretive appendices are integrated, and the original proof and limitations appendices are retained under new labels.

P2.justification: v2 adds four result figures, including three-dataset panels and a five-panel learning-rate sweep, to v1's text-and-equation presentation. The document is also reformatted into an ICLR layout with changed typography, headers, text width, and equation placement. No tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the retained theory easier to assess through empirical checks, implementation details, richer research positioning, and local mathematical corrections. The gain is limited by inconsistent sample counts in Appendix A.1, conflicting Figure 4 slope values, and the acknowledged mismatch with theoretical scaling. The new experiments provide useful evidence, but do not establish the decisive quantitative validation suggested by the abstract.
